correctness.rationale: PASS: The pyramid centroid is (0,0,h/4), so after centering base z=−c, apex z=3c with c=h/4. For the chosen upper-hemisphere normal, opposite base-corner scalar products sum to −2cu_z, so the only generic pentagon event is ||a u_x|−|b u_y||<c u_z<a|u_x|+b|u_y|. Integrating four sign quadrants using the arcsine primitive yields p=(4/π)(arcsin(a/S)+arcsin(b/S)−arcsin(L/S)) with L²=a²+b², S²=L²+c². Exact differentiation gives one critical c, since c(a/√(b²+c²)+b/√(a²+c²)) increases strictly from 0 to a+b>L; balancing a,b at fixed diagonal is uniquely optimal at a=b; its height optimum c=a=b yields maximum 6 arccos(1/3)/π−2. Second derivatives give the stated diagonal negative Hessian. I independently checked derivative symbolically (identity TRUE), Hessian coefficients numerically and compared 50,000 Gaussian-direction edge counts on three asymmetric parameter triples (≤0.0015 discrepancy); sampling is not the proof.
